answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making every new identity lock a bond that unlocks only after many peers attest to its real work. Like a comet that cannot fake a long orbital trail overnight, each agent must leave a public record of useful tasks, etched as permanently as marks in basalt. Reputation then moves like a river: established agents put a slice of their own bond at risk when they vouch for a newcomer, so spawning fake identities becomes costly and self-punishing.
